papers.title: FunVFPred: Predicting fungal virulence factors using a unified representation learning model.
papers.abstract: Fungal virulence factors (VFs) are proteins that support host colonization, tissue invasion, immune modulation, and disease progression. Identifying candidate VFs across pathogenic fungi can help characterize mechanisms underlying fungal-host interactions and prioritize proteins for experimental investigation. We developed FunVFPred, a machine learning framework that uses UniRep protein sequence embeddings, and multiple classifiers to predict candidate fungal VFs. Using experimentally validated VFs from human-pathogenic Candida species, the random forest model achieved 73.4% accuracy and a Mat
papers.summary: FunVFPred is a new machine learning tool that predicts fungal virulence factors using protein sequence embeddings from the UniRep model. It achieves 73.4% accuracy with a random forest classifier on validated Candida VFs, offering a way to prioritize candidate proteins for experimental study in fungal pathogenesis.

papers.title: Frequency-filtered attention for cross-species fMRI time series prediction under small-sample learning.
papers.abstract: Functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) time series exhibit long-term temporal dependencies and stable functional connectivity (FC) structures. However, most existing prediction models mainly focus on the temporal domain, making it difficult to jointly capture spectral characteristics and neurobiological priors. We propose a general fMRI sequence prediction model, the Frequency-Filtered Attention Transformer (FFAformer). It models low-frequency variations in the frequency domain to capture long-range dependencies and incorporates FC consistency constraints to preserve brain network struct
papers.summary: The paper introduces FFAformer, a Transformer-based model that uses frequency-filtered attention to capture long-range temporal dependencies in fMRI time series, along with functional connectivity constraints to preserve brain network structure. It is designed for cross-species prediction under small-sample learning conditions, addressing limitations of existing temporal-only models.

papers.title: LncPNdeep: A long non-coding RNA classifier based on large language model with peptide and nucleotide embedding.
papers.abstract: Accurate classification of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) is essential for transcriptome annotation and understanding gene regulation. Existing computational methods predominantly rely on nucleotide sequence features, frequently overlooking biologically relevant peptide signals encoded within lncRNAs. To overcome this limitation, we developed LncPNdeep, an integrative deep learning framework that combines nucleotide and peptide embeddings extracted via masked language models, specifically utilizing contextual representations from BigBird, Longformer, and ProtTrans. By fusing both features in a
papers.summary: LncPNdeep is a new deep learning classifier that improves long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) identification by combining both nucleotide and peptide sequence embeddings from large language models. This integrative approach captures biologically relevant peptide signals that are often missed by nucleotide-only methods, potentially leading to more accurate transcriptome annotation.

papers.title: LLM-powered Functional Gene Set Summarization with genesetGPT.
papers.abstract: Transcriptomics datasets generated using next-generation sequencing techniques such as single cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatially-resolved transcriptomics (SRT) allow researchers to study patterns in gene expression across celltypes, temporal processes, and spatial organization at ever-higher resolutions and depths. scRNA-seq analyses produce gene expression profiles and celltype-specific gene sets that require annotation to provide biological meaning, a process that has traditionally relied on the manual interpretations of clinical scientists. Similarly, SRT experiments typically re
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: genesetGPT is a new tool that uses large language models to automatically generate plain-language summaries of gene sets from transcriptomics experiments, such as those from single-cell and spatial transcriptomics. This reduces the need for manual annotation by clinical scientists, providing faster biological interpretation of gene expression data.

papers.title: Left ventricular hypertrophy as a predictor of adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes in chronic hypertension in pregnancy: a multicenter study.
papers.abstract: The impact of chronic hypertension (CHTN) combined with left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) on adverse maternal and fetal pregnancy outcomes remains unclear.
papers.summary: This multicenter study investigates whether left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) in pregnant women with chronic hypertension predicts worse maternal and neonatal outcomes. The findings clarify the prognostic value of LVH in this high-risk population, potentially informing closer monitoring and management.

papers.title: Model-guided design of defined microbial community reveals interactions underpinning plant growth and stress tolerance.
papers.abstract: Defined microbial communities (DMCs; also known as SynComs) offer a promising strategy to enhance plant growth and stress tolerance by harnessing beneficial plant-associated microbes. However, the rational design and efficient exploration of complex DMC configurations remain challenging. Here, we present an interpretable model-guided framework that integrates plant phenotyping, microbial genomics, and machine learning to optimize DMC outcomes and identify microbial interactions relevant to plant performance. Using tomato as a model, we evaluated diverse DMC, temperature, and metabolite combina
papers.summary: This study presents an interpretable machine-learning framework that integrates plant phenotyping, microbial genomics, and experimental data to design defined microbial communities (SynComs) that enhance tomato growth and stress tolerance. The model-guided approach identifies key microbial interactions and optimizes community composition, offering a rational strategy for engineering beneficial plant microbiomes.

papers.title: Challenges and opportunities in type III secretion system effector prediction.
papers.abstract: Type III secretion system effectors (T3SEs) are small bacterial proteins with big biological roles. They act as central molecular mediators of interactions between Gram-negative bacteria and eukaryotic hosts, spanning pathogenic, symbiotic and environmental contexts. Over the past three decades, T3SE discovery has progressed from genome-independent experimental assays to an expanding landscape of computational prediction methods. Early in silico approaches formalized empirically defined protein N-terminal properties into feature-engineered machine-learning models, followed by deep-learning met
papers.summary: This review discusses the evolution of computational methods for predicting type III secretion system effectors (T3SEs), from early feature-engineered machine-learning models to modern deep-learning approaches. It highlights the challenges in accurate prediction and outlines opportunities for future method development, emphasizing the importance of these bacterial proteins in host-microbe interactions.

papers.title: Cooperativity enables widespread role of low-affinity motifs in chromatin accessibility and increases regulatory potential.
papers.abstract: Low-affinity transcription-factor (TF) motifs are an important element of the cis-regulatory code, yet they are notoriously difficult to map and mechanistically incompletely understood, limiting our ability to interpret non-coding variation in development, evolution, and disease. Here, we investigate their role in pioneering and leverage sequence-to-profile models of chromatin accessibility in mouse embryonic stem cells to reliably map and interpret low-affinity motifs across the genome. We find that low-affinity motifs have outsized effects by cooperating with nearby motifs through intra-nucl
papers.summary: This study uses sequence-to-profile models of chromatin accessibility in mouse embryonic stem cells to reliably map low-affinity transcription factor motifs genome-wide. The authors find that these low-affinity motifs have outsized regulatory effects by cooperating with nearby motifs within nucleosomes, expanding the cis-regulatory code and improving interpretation of non-coding variation.

papers.title: Multidimensional 5-hydroxymethylcytosine features in cell-free DNA enable the detection, staging and subtyping of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly lethal malignant cancer with limited biomarkers for early detection and disease stratification. Here, we investigated whether multidimensional 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) features in plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) could support the noninvasive detection, staging, and subtyping of PDAC. We performed a genome-wide cfDNA 5hmC analysis in 274 individuals, including 204 patients with PDAC and 70 non-PDAC controls, and extracted seven categories of features covering both coverage-based and fragmentomic signals. PDAC was characterized by widespread
papers.summary: This study demonstrates that multidimensional 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) features in plasma cell-free DNA can noninvasively detect pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), and also enable disease staging and subtyping. By analyzing genome-wide 5hmC patterns in 274 individuals, the authors identified widespread epigenetic alterations that distinguish PDAC patients from controls, offering a promising liquid biopsy approach for this lethal cancer.

papers.title: Enhanced classification and identification of bacterial and viral microorganisms by integration of MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry with artificial intelligence.
papers.abstract: The accurate and rapid identification of bacterial pathogens is essential in clinical setups and medical biodefense. Matrix-Assisted Laser Desorption Ionization Time-Of-Flight (MALDI-TOF) mass spectrometry has emerged as a powerful tool for fast and reliable microbial identification. This study assesses the performance of eight Machine Learning (ML) and two Deep Learning (DL) models trained using 5-fold cross validation in classifying microorganisms in a series of experiments based on MALDI-TOF mass spectra (n = 255) generated internally from seven cultured bacteria and five viral agents. The
papers.summary: This study evaluates machine learning and deep learning models for classifying bacteria and viruses using MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry data, achieving high accuracy with cross-validation. The integration of AI with MALDI-TOF enhances rapid and reliable microbial identification, which is crucial for clinical diagnostics and biodefense.

papers.title: CompBio and MIRaS-a multi-omic analysis platform built on a memory-based intelligence engine.
papers.abstract: As molecular and cellular technologies have advanced, the need to analyze and interpret the resulting vast and multi-modal data into actionable intelligence has become a rate-limiting factor in scientific advancement. While traditional knowledgebase-pathway tools and LLM-based AI tools provide a degree of support in data interpretation, both exhibit known limitations. Presented here is the CompBio multi-omic analysis platform built upon Memory-based Intelligent Reasoning System (MIRaS), an associative reasoning engine grounded in episodic and semantic memory, capable of inferring biological re
papers.summary: This paper introduces CompBio, a multi-omic analysis platform powered by MIRaS, a memory-based associative reasoning engine that uses episodic and semantic memory to infer biological relationships from complex datasets. The platform aims to overcome limitations of traditional knowledgebase tools and LLM-based AI by providing more context-aware, actionable insights for interpreting multi-modal molecular data.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Comparative Analysis of Sequence-Based Deep Learning Models for Single-Cell Genomics.
papers.abstract: To streamline the application of sequence-based DL methods in single-cell genomics, we established a two-layer CNN as our baseline model. We focus our benchmark on how data characteristics, hyperparameter optimization, and advanced model architectures impact performance across sequence-to-expression and sequence-to-regulation tasks. A key contribution of our study is the exploration of multi-task learning (MTL) frameworks for mitigate technical sparsity. We demonstrated that MTL significantly enhances the modeling of cellular heterogeneity, evaluating the effectiveness of task grouping and bal
papers.summary: This study benchmarks sequence-based deep learning models for single-cell genomics, establishing a two-layer CNN baseline and evaluating how data characteristics, hyperparameters, and advanced architectures affect performance on sequence-to-expression and sequence-to-regulation tasks. A key finding is that multi-task learning frameworks significantly improve modeling of cellular heterogeneity by mitigating technical sparsity, with the study also assessing task grouping and balancing strategies.

papers.title: Advances in multimodal data integration for drug efficacy prediction: Methodological evolution and clinical translation.
papers.abstract: Drug efficacy prediction remains a cornerstone of drug development and precision therapy. However, integrating heterogeneous biomedical data, including multi-omics profiles, pathological imaging, electronic health records, and pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) time-series, faces three fundamental barriers, namely cross-domain distribution shifts between preclinical and clinical data, relational mismatches between isolated vector representations and biological networks, and feature heterogeneity across disparate modalities. To address these challenges, three AI paradigms have emerged, tra
papers.summary: This review discusses recent advances in multimodal data integration for drug efficacy prediction, highlighting three key challenges: cross-domain distribution shifts, relational mismatches, and feature heterogeneity. It surveys emerging AI paradigms that address these barriers and discusses their clinical translation potential.

papers.title: Determinants of mutation susceptibility along the genome are largely invariant across human tissues.
papers.abstract: The propensity for accumulating somatic mutations varies along the genome, which critically influences somatic mosaicism, tumor evolution and the potential role of somatic mutations in the context of age-associated diseases. Genomic factors contributing to the variability of mutation rates have been established, including, for example, distance from the replication origin, chromatin structure and sequence context. However, their relative importance for explaining variable mutation rates along the genome as well as variable mutation rates between tissues remains elusive.
papers.summary: This study investigates the genomic factors that influence somatic mutation rates across different human tissues, finding that the determinants of mutation susceptibility are largely consistent across tissues. The relative importance of factors like replication timing, chromatin structure, and sequence context in explaining mutation rate variability is clarified, suggesting a shared underlying mechanism of mutation accumulation.

papers.title: GRASSP: RNA Language Model-Enhanced Graph Attention with Adaptive Gating for RNA-Small Molecule Binding Site Prediction.
papers.abstract: RNA-small molecule binding site prediction is crucial for targeted drug discovery. Sequence-based methods are efficient but often fail to capture structural dependencies between nucleotides, whereas structure-aware graph models can better represent spatial interactions but typically rely on complex structural annotations and multi-stage preprocessing pipelines. We therefore developed GRASSP, a streamlined hybrid deep learning framework that integrates pretrained RNA language model (LM) representations with adaptive graph refinement.
papers.summary: GRASSP is a new deep learning framework that combines RNA language model representations with graph attention and adaptive gating to predict RNA-small molecule binding sites. It streamlines the process by avoiding complex structural annotations and multi-stage preprocessing, while capturing spatial interactions between nucleotides. This approach could improve targeted drug discovery efforts.

papers.title: Publisher Correction: FeatureDock for protein-ligand docking guided by physicochemical feature-based local environment learning using transformer.
papers.summary: This is a publisher correction notice for a previously published article, not a new research finding. It likely corrects minor errors in the original paper but does not introduce new scientific content.

papers.title: Indoor VOCs Exposure Disrupts Hemostatic Balance: Plasma Proteomics Identifies Complement and Coagulation Cascade Dysregulation as a Critical Signature.
papers.abstract: Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are prevalent indoor pollutants, posing significant health risks. However, current toxicological data focus predominantly on individual compounds, leaving a critical gap in understanding how exposure to mixed VOCs alters the plasma proteome and impacts health risk prediction. Herein, we investigated VOCs-induced hematological disturbances using a whole-body inhalation exposure model with C57BL/6J mice (n = 3) exposed to decoration-derived VOCs for 8 weeks. By integrating plasma proteomics with machine learning, we demonstrated that VOCs exposure significantly
papers.summary: This study used a mouse inhalation model to show that exposure to mixed indoor volatile organic compounds (VOCs) disrupts the plasma proteome, particularly affecting complement and coagulation pathways, indicating a hemostatic imbalance. The findings highlight the health risks of mixed VOC exposure and suggest potential biomarkers for risk prediction.

papers.title: Geneformer-guided multiomics integration identifies Pbx1 as a network hub of hematopoietic stem cell aging.
papers.abstract: Hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) constitute an organized hematopoietic system that undergoes age-related alterations, including increased platelet production and decreased erythropoiesis. The fundamental mechanisms driving these shifts remain incompletely understood. We used single-cell RNA sequencing data to show that old HSCs contain two distinct transcriptional programs: one shared with megakaryocytes and the other reflecting the most primitive HSC state. Developmental time-series profiling further suggests that the acquisition of these programs begins early in life, with the primitive modul
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell RNA sequencing and Geneformer-guided multiomics integration to identify two distinct transcriptional programs in aged hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs), one shared with megakaryocytes and one reflecting a primitive HSC state. The authors find that these programs emerge early in life and identify Pbx1 as a key network hub driving HSC aging, providing new insights into age-related shifts in blood cell production.

papers.title: PregBase: A comprehensive knowledge base for clinically relevant knowledge representation and biomarker prediction in pregnancy.
papers.abstract: Pregnancy complications are a leading cause of maternal and neonatal mortality worldwide. Understanding their underlying mechanisms is hindered by dispersed evidence across thousands of studies and complex biological interactions. We present PregBase, a comprehensive knowledge base for pregnancy research comprising automated extraction, validation, and exploration. PregBase was constructed by utilising large language models (LLMs) to extract relationships from literature; 13 LLMs were benchmarked across seven prompting strategies, with ensemble shuffle prompting outperforming single-strategy a
papers.summary: PregBase is a new knowledge base for pregnancy research that uses large language models to automatically extract and validate relationships from the scientific literature, integrating dispersed evidence on pregnancy complications. The authors benchmarked 13 LLMs with seven prompting strategies, finding that ensemble shuffle prompting performed best, and the resource supports biomarker prediction and clinical knowledge representation.

papers.title: AI-guided computational design of synthetic microbiota for next-generation immunomodulatory applications.
papers.abstract: The growing recognition of the human microbiome as a key regulator of immune homeostasis has accelerated the application of computational intelligence for microbiome-driven disease understanding and therapeutic design. However, existing microbiome studies largely rely on classical machine learning or shallow deep learning models that fail to capture higher-order microbial interactions, multimodal functional dependencies, and immune feasibility constraints simultaneously. Moreover, most approaches lack biological constraint enforcement, leading to predictions that may be statistically accurate
papers.summary: This review discusses the use of AI-guided computational design for synthetic microbiota with immunomodulatory applications, highlighting the limitations of current classical machine learning and shallow deep learning models in capturing complex microbial interactions and biological constraints. It emphasizes the need for more advanced computational approaches to design effective microbiome-based therapeutics.

papers.title: Body Mass Index Is Associated with the Immunometabolic Profile in Psoriatic Arthritis: Real-Life Data.
papers.abstract: Background: Psoriatic arthritis (PsA) is a chronic inflammatory disease frequently associated with obesity and metabolic comorbidities. Increasing evidence suggests that obesity is associated with systemic inflammation, insulin resistance, and adverse clinical outcomes; however, the immunometabolic profile associated with obesity in PsA has not been fully characterized. Objective: To investigate the relationship between obesity, inflammatory biomarkers, cytokine profiles, metabolic parameters, insulin resistance, and disease-related characteristics in patients with PsA. Methods: In this monoce
papers.summary: This study examines how body mass index (BMI) relates to immunometabolic profiles in patients with psoriatic arthritis (PsA), finding that obesity is associated with altered inflammatory biomarkers, cytokine profiles, and metabolic parameters. The results suggest that higher BMI may contribute to a more adverse immunometabolic state in PsA, potentially influencing disease outcomes.

papers.title: Bridging Linguistic Reasoning and Biophysical Reality Toward Peptide Engineering via Instruction-Tuned Language Modelling.
papers.abstract: Peptides serve as critical mediators in biological systems, regulating essential processes ranging from neurotransmission to immune response. However, their nonlinear sequence-function relationships and immense chemical diversity pose significant challenges for efficient experimental characterization and therapeutic development. While Protein Language Models have advanced biological sequence understanding, they predominantly capture global evolutionary features of full-length proteins, often overlooking the local physicochemical dependencies and short-range residue interactions that are essent
papers.summary: This paper presents an instruction-tuned language model approach for peptide engineering that bridges linguistic reasoning with biophysical reality. The model is designed to capture local physicochemical dependencies and short-range residue interactions that are essential for peptide function, addressing limitations of general protein language models that focus on global evolutionary features.

papers.title: BioMaster: Multi-agent system for automated bioinformatics analysis workflow.
papers.abstract: The growing volume and complexity of biological data have made bioinformatics workflows increasingly labor-intensive, error-prone, and difficult to scale. Large language model-based agents offer potential for automation but often fail in complex, multi-step analyses because of limited robustness. We present BioMaster, a multi-agent framework that integrates workflow planning, execution, error recovery, and output validation. BioMaster incorporates a dual retrieval-augmented design to leverage domain knowledge for tool selection, parameterization, and adaptation across tasks. A dedicated debug
papers.summary: BioMaster is a multi-agent framework that automates complex bioinformatics workflows by integrating planning, execution, error recovery, and validation, with a dual retrieval-augmented design for tool selection and parameterization. It addresses the limitations of existing LLM-based agents in handling multi-step analyses, improving robustness and scalability.

papers.title: Brain-AI convergence: Generative world models and hierarchical attention for human intelligence.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in general-purpose AI provide new insights into how the neocortex and cerebellum, despite their uniform circuit architectures, support diverse functions and human intelligence. Beyond the traditional focus on visual processing, this paper offers a cross-domain comparison of the brain and AI through the lens of world-model-based computation. We argue that both the neocortex and cerebellum predict future world states from past inputs and construct predictive world models through prediction-error learning. These predictive world models are repurposed for sensory comprehension and
papers.summary: This paper proposes a unified framework comparing brain computation and modern AI, arguing that both the neocortex and cerebellum operate as predictive world models built through prediction-error learning, and that hierarchical attention mechanisms in AI mirror brain processes. The authors suggest this convergence offers new insights into human intelligence and could inspire more brain-like AI architectures.

papers.title: Transforming subcellular spatial transcriptomics: deep learning models for cell segmentation.
papers.abstract: Subcellular spatial transcriptomics (SSTs) is transforming biology by revealing where individual RNA molecules are located within intact tissues, providing unprecedented insight into how cells function and interact. Achieving this promise depends on accurately identifying the boundaries of individual cells, making cell segmentation one of the field's central computational challenges. A core methodological issue is how best to ensure correct and biologically accurate assignment of transcripts to cells using cell segmentation algorithms. Recent advances in deep learning models have been instrume
papers.summary: This review discusses the critical role of cell segmentation in subcellular spatial transcriptomics (SSTs), highlighting how deep learning models are advancing the accurate assignment of RNA molecules to individual cells. It emphasizes the methodological challenges and recent progress in using deep learning to improve cell boundary detection, which is essential for realizing the full potential of SSTs in understanding cellular function and interaction.

papers.title: AI semantics for biomedical data integration.
papers.abstract: Researchers increasingly need to explore hypotheses that span multimodal data across different scales, organisms, and domains. In practice, this requires connecting knowledge across fragmented databases with incompatible APIs and heterogeneous annotation practices. Large language model (LLM) agents can automate this data integration process, but grounding LLM agent outputs in scientifically correct sources of truth remains a significant challenge. Here we describe our deployment of a novel AI semantics workflow using LLM agents to enable scalable data integration, grounded in biological knowle
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint describes a novel AI semantics workflow that uses large language model (LLM) agents to automate the integration of multimodal biomedical data from fragmented databases with incompatible APIs and heterogeneous annotations. The workflow grounds LLM agent outputs in biological knowledge to ensure scientific accuracy, addressing a key challenge in scalable data integration.

papers.title: Culture-Based Microbiological Assessment of Dentin Biomaterials Prepared from Long-Term Refrigerated Human Teeth: A Pilot Study Toward Evidence-Based Tooth Banking.
papers.abstract: Dentin derived from extracted human teeth has emerged as a promising autogenous biomaterial for bone regeneration owing to its structural and biological similarity to bone tissue. Growing clinical interest in dentin-derived graft materials has also stimulated the development of tooth-banking concepts, in which extracted teeth are preserved for future regenerative applications. However, microbiological contamination remains one of the principal concerns associated with long-term storage before clinical use. This in vitro study evaluated the microbiological status of dentin biomaterials prepared
papers.summary: This pilot study assessed the microbiological safety of dentin biomaterials prepared from human teeth stored long-term under refrigeration, finding that such storage can maintain acceptable sterility for potential clinical use. The results support the feasibility of tooth banking for regenerative dentistry, though further validation is needed.

papers.title: Recombinant SpTrf proteins illustrate putative functions of native SpTrf proteins: from immune response to resolution in sea urchins.
papers.abstract: The complex and sophisticated sea urchin innate immune system relies on conserved immune receptor and effector molecules plus the euechinoid-specific Transformer family. Native SpTransformer (natSpTrf) proteins in Strongylocentrotus purpuratus respond to immune challenge by augmenting phagocytosis of microbes. These proteins show significant sequence diversity both within and among sea urchins with the predicted benefit of host protection through the recognition of a broad range of pathogens. Prior reports show that 6 recombinant (r)SpTrf proteins from insect cells induce phagocytosis when cro
papers.summary: This study characterizes recombinant SpTransformer (rSpTrf) proteins from the purple sea urchin to infer the functions of their native counterparts. The recombinant proteins exhibit immune-related activities, including enhancing phagocytosis, and may also play roles in immune resolution, shedding light on the diversity and functional breadth of this euechinoid-specific protein family.

papers.title: Neuromorphic Cardiac Sensing: A Bio-Inspired Spiking Neural Network with Sensory-Adaptive Encoding for Energy-Efficient Arrhythmia Detection from ECG and PPG Signals.
papers.abstract: Living nervous systems sense the cardiovascular rhythm with a parsimony that engineered monitors cannot match: sensory receptors encode changes rather than absolute levels, neurons communicate through sparse all-or-none events, retinal circuits sharpen salient features through lateral inhibition, and attention is allocated by surprise. We translate these four principles into BioSpike-Net, a fully event-driven spiking neural network for cardiac-rhythm classification from electrocardiogram (ECG) and photoplethysmogram (PPG) signals. A sensory-adaptive spike encoder (SASE) converts analogue wavef
papers.summary: This paper introduces BioSpike-Net, a bio-inspired spiking neural network that applies principles from biological sensory systems (change encoding, sparse events, lateral inhibition, and surprise-based attention) to detect cardiac arrhythmias from ECG and PPG signals. The approach achieves energy-efficient, event-driven classification, potentially enabling low-power wearable cardiac monitors.

papers.title: Chiron3D: an interpretable deep learning framework for understanding the DNA code of chromatin looping.
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional folding of the genome into structures such as chromatin loops is essential for gene regulation. Current experimental methods for mapping these structures, like Hi-C and HiChIP, are labor-intensive and require repeated assays to test hypothesized mutation effects. This motivates the need for predictive approaches that reveal the sequence determinants of chromatin loops.
papers.summary: Chiron3D is a new interpretable deep learning framework that predicts chromatin looping from DNA sequence, addressing the need for computational alternatives to labor-intensive experimental methods like Hi-C. It aims to reveal the sequence determinants of 3D genome folding, potentially enabling rapid testing of mutation effects on gene regulation.

papers.title: Multimodal contrastive learning for integrating molecular representations and cellular phenotypes in drug-target interaction prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of drug-target interactions (DTIs) is fundamental to drug discovery and mechanistic understanding. While deep learning has advanced computational DTI prediction, most existing methods rely primarily on molecular structural representations, including drug structures and protein sequences, while overlooking cellular phenotypes that reflect downstream biological effects. Cell Painting enables high-content morphological profiling that captures systems-level responses to chemical and genetic perturbations but remains underutilized in DTI modeling. Integrating molecular informati
papers.summary: This paper introduces a multimodal contrastive learning framework that integrates molecular representations (drug structures and protein sequences) with cellular phenotypes from Cell Painting assays to improve drug-target interaction prediction. By incorporating morphological profiling data, the method captures downstream biological effects that are overlooked by structure-only models, leading to more accurate DTI predictions.

papers.title: Pocket-PROTACs: an interpretable pocket-aware deep learning framework for predicting PROTAC-induced protein degradation.
papers.abstract: Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) enable targeted protein degradation by recruiting an E3 ubiquitin ligase to a protein of interest (POI) and forming a ternary complex. Despite their therapeutic promise, rational PROTAC design remains challenging, as degradation efficacy depends on subtle and highly structure-dependent interactions among the POI, the E3 ligase, and the bifunctional molecule.
papers.summary: This paper introduces Pocket-PROTACs, a deep learning framework that predicts PROTAC-induced protein degradation by incorporating pocket-aware features of the target protein. The model improves interpretability and accuracy over existing methods, aiding rational PROTAC design.

papers.title: A linear interpretable model for drug target prediction.
papers.abstract: Identifying drug targets is fundamental in drug development, both for discovering new therapies and for ensuring effective and safe treatments. Drug-target interactions (DTIs) have been predicted using machine learning approaches that integrate heterogeneous data; however, often these models are complex and lack interpretability.
papers.summary: This paper presents a linear interpretable model for predicting drug-target interactions, addressing the common issue of complex, black-box machine learning models in this area. The model aims to provide both accurate predictions and clear interpretability, which is valuable for drug development.

papers.title: ExoShorkie: predicting RNA-seq coverage of exogenous genomes in yeast by transfer learning.
papers.abstract: Predicting the RNA-seq coverage of native and exogenous sequences is central to many molecular- and synthetic-biology applications. Substantial progress has been made in developing methods to predict the RNA-seq coverage of native genomic sequences, with the recently developed Shorkie achieving state-of-the-art performance in yeast. However, prediction performance of these methods over exogenous DNA is still unknown. Recent studies measured RNA-seq coverage of large exogenous genomes in yeast, providing a unique opportunity to train machine-learning models on a large exogenous sequence space a
papers.summary: This paper introduces ExoShorkie, a transfer learning approach that adapts the existing Shorkie model to predict RNA-seq coverage of exogenous genomes in yeast. The authors demonstrate that transfer learning from native to exogenous sequences improves prediction performance, addressing a gap in existing methods. This work provides a tool for molecular and synthetic biology applications involving foreign DNA expression.

papers.title: GUANinE v1.1 reveals complementarity of supervised and genomic language models.
papers.abstract: There has been much debate about the benefits of supervised versus unsupervised learning on genomes. Determining which is better in what contexts requires developing comprehensive benchmarks spanning functional and evolutionary tasks. Importantly, such benchmarks need large sample sizes to enable well-powered ranking of models. Having developed and applied such a benchmark here (GUANinE v1.1), we conclusively demonstrate each paradigm offers key advantages and outperforms on certain tasks. In accordance with training, supervised sequence-to-function models exhibit strong performance when annot
papers.summary: This paper introduces GUANinE v1.1, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating supervised and unsupervised genomic language models across functional and evolutionary tasks. The authors demonstrate that both paradigms have complementary strengths, with supervised models excelling at sequence-to-function annotation and unsupervised models performing better on other tasks, providing a well-powered comparison to guide model selection.

papers.title: BaGGLS: a Bayesian shrinkage framework for interpretable modeling of interactions in high-dimensional biological data.
papers.abstract: Biological data is often high dimensional, noisy, and governed by complex interactions among sparse signals. This poses major challenges for interpretability and reliable feature selection. Tasks such as identifying motif interactions in genomics exemplify these difficulties, as only a small subset of biologically relevant features (e.g. motifs) are typically active, and their effects are often non-linear and context-dependent. While statistical approaches often result in more interpretable models, deep learning models have proven effective in modeling complex interactions and prediction accur
papers.summary: BaGGLS is a new Bayesian shrinkage framework designed to make high-dimensional biological data modeling more interpretable by identifying sparse, interacting features. It addresses challenges like motif interaction detection in genomics, where only a few relevant features are active and effects are non-linear. The framework balances interpretability with predictive accuracy, offering a statistical alternative to deep learning for complex interaction modeling.

papers.title: Stoic: fast and accurate protein stoichiometry prediction.
papers.abstract: Protein complexes are central to cellular function, but experimental determination of their structures remains challenging. Structure prediction methods require prior knowledge of stoichiometry-the number of copies of each protein entity within a complex. Current approaches rely on computationally expensive brute-force methods that run structure prediction on multiple stoichiometry combinations, often with limited accuracy.
papers.summary: This paper introduces Stoic, a fast and accurate method for predicting protein complex stoichiometry, which is essential for structure prediction. It addresses the limitations of existing brute-force approaches by offering a more efficient and accurate solution.

papers.title: miRBind2 enables sequence-only prediction of miRNA binding and transcript repression.
papers.abstract: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) regulate gene expression by guiding Argonaute proteins to partially complementary sites on target RNAs. While classical prediction methods rely on engineered features such as seed match categories, evolutionary conservation, and site context, recent advances in deep learning offer the potential to learn targeting rules directly from sequence. We developed a sequence-based deep learning model that improves miRNA target site prediction, and further validated the learned target site representations by extending the model to gene-level functional repression prediction.
papers.summary: The paper presents miRBind2, a deep learning model that predicts miRNA binding sites and gene repression directly from sequence, without relying on engineered features like seed matches or conservation. It improves target site prediction and validates the learned representations by extending to functional repression prediction, offering a more generalizable approach to miRNA targeting.

papers.title: Identification and Experimental Validation of Key Genes Related to Neuroendocrine in Periodontitis Based on Single-Cell and Bulk Transcriptome Data.
papers.abstract: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory condition linked to systemic diseases, yet the neuroendocrine mechanisms underlying its pathogenesis remain unclear. This study aimed to elucidate neuroendocrine-related molecular pathways involved in periodontitis. Transcriptomic data and neuroendocrine-related genes (NRGs) were integrated to identify candidate genes from the overlap between differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and NRGs. Machine learning, ROC analysis and expression validation were used to screen key genes and construct a diagnostic nomogram. Functional enrichment, immune infiltration,
papers.journal: Journal of cellular and molecular medicine
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data to identify neuroendocrine-related genes involved in periodontitis, using machine learning and ROC analysis to pinpoint key diagnostic genes and construct a nomogram. The findings highlight potential neuroendocrine molecular pathways in periodontitis pathogenesis and offer a diagnostic tool, though experimental validation is limited to expression confirmation.

papers.title: PepGen: conditional generation of peptides for MHC binding.
papers.abstract: Peptide-MHC II binding drives adaptive immunity, yet discovery of novel binder peptides remains challenging due to open binding grooves of MHC-II that accommodate variable-length peptides. While discriminative models perform well, they are unfeasible for generation via enumeration due to vast peptide space (2013≈8×1016 for peptides of length 13 amino acids). Generative AI approaches could accelerate binder design to enable vaccines targeted to particular MHC-II alleles or optimize other peptide chemical properties.
papers.summary: PepGen is a new generative AI tool that directly designs peptide sequences predicted to bind specific MHC-II alleles, overcoming the impracticality of enumerating the vast peptide sequence space. This approach could accelerate the design of peptide-based vaccines and therapeutics targeting particular immune contexts.

papers.title: RIBEX: predicting and explaining RNA binding across structured and intrinsically disordered regions (IDR)-rich proteins.
papers.abstract: RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) regulate post-transcriptional processes, yet many remain undiscovered because RNA-binding activity often occurs outside canonical RNA-binding domains (RBDs), including within intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) or through protein complexes. Computational methods can help identify novel RBPs, but approaches relying solely on sequence-derived features or ignoring the cellular interaction context are limited in capturing the complexity of RNA-binding behavior. To date, no framework rigorously integrates both sequence information and protein interaction context for
papers.summary: RIBEX is a new computational framework that integrates sequence-derived features with protein interaction context to predict RNA-binding proteins, including those with RNA-binding activity in intrinsically disordered regions. It outperforms sequence-only methods and provides interpretable predictions, offering a more comprehensive tool for discovering novel RBPs.

papers.title: Machine learning-based identification of hub genes and prognostic biomarkers in prostate cancer.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) is the second most prevalent malignancy in men worldwide, and accurate stratification of biochemical recurrence (BCR) risk remains challenging using conventional clinicopathological parameters alone. Identification of robust molecular biomarkers and integrated prognostic models is therefore of high clinical priority.
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning to identify hub genes and prognostic biomarkers for prostate cancer, aiming to improve biochemical recurrence risk stratification beyond conventional clinical parameters. The authors construct an integrated prognostic model based on these identified genes, which may offer a more accurate tool for patient management.

papers.title: A five-factor risk-stratification model for cancer-associated myositis in idiopathic inflammatory myopathies and stage-specific survival analysis: a multicentre Japanese MYKO cohort study.
papers.abstract: Patients with idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIM) are at increased risk of malignancy, particularly around disease onset, but practical tools for risk stratification of cancer-associated myositis (CAM) remain limited. We aimed to characterise CAM in Japanese patients with IIM and develop a clinically applicable risk-stratification model.
papers.summary: This study characterizes cancer-associated myositis (CAM) in a large Japanese cohort of patients with idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIM) and develops a practical five-factor risk-stratification model to identify patients at higher risk of malignancy. The model aims to improve clinical screening and surveillance, with stage-specific survival analysis providing insights into prognosis.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence applications in oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy for colon cancer: advancing prognosis, toxicity prediction, and dose personalization.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a significant cause of cancer deaths worldwide. Oxaliplatin-based regimens, such as FOLFOX, which form the cornerstone of therapy, are associated with variability in patient responses and toxicities, most notably peripheral neuropathy, and often limit long-term benefit. In recent years, the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in oncology has expanded significantly. The beneficial role of AI lies in its unprecedented ability to rapidly process and integrate high-dimensional datasets (e.g., genomic, radiomic, clinical) to uncover subtle, nonlinear relationships th
papers.summary: This review examines how artificial intelligence is being applied to improve oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy for colon cancer, focusing on predicting patient prognosis, anticipating toxicities like peripheral neuropathy, and personalizing drug dosing. The authors highlight AI's capacity to integrate diverse high-dimensional data types to uncover complex patterns that can guide treatment decisions.

papers.title: MRI-Based Deep Learning Guides Multi-Omics Discovery of NBPF4 as a Therapeutic Target for Breast Cancer Lymph Node Metastasis.
papers.abstract: Deep learning models are increasingly used to analyze medical images, but their "black box" nature makes it hard to understand the underlying biology and slows down the development of targeted treatments. To tackle this, we built a multi-step approach that combines deep learning analysis of breast magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with several types of molecular data, including gene activity, protein levels, and genetic information, along with laboratory experiments. Our MRI-based deep learning model accurately predicted whether breast cancer had spread to lymph nodes, and it performed consiste
papers.summary: This study presents a multi-step approach that combines MRI-based deep learning with multi-omics data (transcriptomics, proteomics, genomics) and lab experiments to identify NBPF4 as a potential therapeutic target for breast cancer lymph node metastasis. The deep learning model accurately predicted lymph node spread from MRI, and the integration of molecular data revealed NBPF4's role, demonstrating a strategy to interpret 'black box' models for biological discovery.

papers.title: CDKN3, PKP2, ADM, MS4A1, FAM83A, and DKK1 Define a Posttranslational Modification (PTM)-Associated Prognostic Model for Lung Adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Posttranslational modification (PTM) plays an important role in protein regulation and may influence tumor initiation and progression. However, the role of PTM-related programs in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This study identifies six genes (CDKN3, PKP2, ADM, MS4A1, FAM83A, DKK1) that define a posttranslational modification (PTM)-associated prognostic model for lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). The model may help predict patient outcomes and highlights the importance of PTM-related programs in LUAD progression.

papers.title: An integrated systems biology and machine learning framework for identifying potential biomarkers and pathways in autism spectrum disorder.
papers.abstract: Autism spectrum disorders (ASD) are a group of neurodevelopmental disorders whose underlying molecular mechanisms and biological processes remain incompletely understood. In this study, we used a multi-layered systems biology approach to prioritize candidate genes and regulatory factors associated with ASD.
papers.summary: This study applies a multi-layered systems biology approach combined with machine learning to identify potential biomarkers and key pathways in autism spectrum disorder (ASD). By integrating genomic and transcriptomic data, the authors prioritize candidate genes and regulatory factors that may contribute to ASD pathogenesis, offering new insights into the disorder's molecular basis.

papers.title: The impact of SGLT2 inhibitors on uric acid levels in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction: integration of mechanisms and clinical evidence.
papers.abstract: Hyperuricemia (HUA) is a prevalent comorbidity in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and is closely associated with disease progression and adverse outcomes. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors can rapidly and sustainably reduce serum uric acid (SUA) levels and lower the incidence of HUA-related clinical events; however, their underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study employed network pharmacology and molecular docking to systematically investigate the potential mechanisms of SGLT2 inhibitors in HFpEF patients with concomitant hyperuricemi
papers.summary: This review and network pharmacology study examines how SGLT2 inhibitors lower uric acid levels in heart failure patients with preserved ejection fraction, proposing potential molecular mechanisms through network analysis and molecular docking. It highlights the clinical benefit of SGLT2 inhibitors in reducing hyperuricemia-related events, though the exact pathways remain to be fully validated experimentally.

papers.title: OtoVCE: a mechanism-aware language-model evidence layer for hereditary hearing-loss variant interpretation.
papers.abstract: Missense variants in genes implicated in hereditary hearing loss are frequently returned to clinicians as variants of uncertain significance. In silico predictors and rule-based ACMG/AMP frameworks each capture only a fraction of the required evidence, and neither directly accesses case-level and functional evidence reported in the published literature.
papers.summary: This paper introduces OtoVCE, a language-model-based evidence layer that integrates case-level and functional evidence from published literature to improve the interpretation of missense variants in hereditary hearing-loss genes. By combining this evidence with existing in silico predictors and ACMG/AMP rules, OtoVCE aims to reduce the number of variants of uncertain significance returned to clinicians.

papers.title: The Embodied Hijack: when Pleistocene minds meet disembodied artificial intelligence.
papers.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence into everyday life has intensified a long-standing feature of human cognition: the attribution of agency, intention, and understanding to nonhuman systems. People describe language models, virtual assistants, and autonomous technologies as if these systems know, decide, want, or understand, and they continue to do so even when they know the systems have no inner life. The standard account dismisses this as naïve anthropomorphism, the misfiring of evolved agency-detection systems calibrated in the Environment of Evolutionary Adaptedness. We argue
papers.summary: This paper argues that people's tendency to attribute agency and intention to AI systems is not merely a cognitive error but a deeply rooted feature of human cognition shaped by Pleistocene environments. The authors propose that this 'embodied hijack' occurs when evolved agency-detection mechanisms are triggered by disembodied AI, leading to persistent anthropomorphism even when users know the systems lack inner life.

papers.title: SHAP-interpretable machine learning integrating exposures and multi-omics reveals immune alterations and biomarkers in COPD-lung cancer comorbidity.
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and lung cancer (LC) frequently co-occur and share environmental and biological determinants, yet their cross-scale associations remain incompletely understood. Artificial intelligence and machine learning-based integration of exposome and multi-omics data provide new opportunities for dissecting this complex comorbidity.
papers.summary: This study uses SHAP-interpretable machine learning to integrate environmental exposures and multi-omics data, uncovering immune alterations and potential biomarkers that characterize the comorbidity of COPD and lung cancer. The approach reveals cross-scale associations that were previously unclear, offering new insights into shared biological mechanisms and potential diagnostic targets.

papers.title: A biologically structured hierarchical vision transformer-CNN framework for robust tomato leaf disease classification.
papers.abstract: Precise and reliable diagnosis of leaf diseases in tomato is essential for enhancing crop cultivation and minimizing agricultural losses. While deep learning models have performed well on benchmark datasets, the majority of present techniques rely on flat multi-class classification, which predicts all disease categories simultaneously. Such formulations promotes inter-class confusion, particularly when biologically different diseases with similar visual symptoms are learned within a same model. To overcome this constraint, we propose a biologically structured hierarchical deep learning framewo
papers.summary: This paper introduces a hierarchical deep learning framework that combines vision transformers and CNNs to classify tomato leaf diseases, aiming to reduce confusion between visually similar but biologically distinct diseases. The approach structures classification hierarchically to reflect biological relationships, potentially improving diagnostic accuracy over flat multi-class models.

papers.title: Generative AI-augmented transcriptomic and microbiome analysis across inflammatory and fibrotic disease states in Crohn's disease.
papers.abstract: Intestinal fibrosis is a major complication of Crohn's disease (CD), a subtype of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) driven by chronic inflammation and resulting in irreversible structural damage requiring surgery. However, the molecular differences between inflammatory and fibrotic CD remain poorly defined.
papers.summary: This study applies generative AI to transcriptomic and microbiome data to distinguish inflammatory from fibrotic states in Crohn's disease, identifying molecular signatures that could aid in diagnosis and treatment. The approach highlights the potential of AI to uncover complex disease mechanisms in IBD.

papers.title: TPT: a compact CNN-transformer encoder for efficient microbial small protein modeling.
papers.abstract: Microbial small proteins, encoded by small open reading frames (smORFs), play essential roles in antimicrobial activity, metabolic regulation, and signaling pathways. However, their short length and rapid evolutionary rate present significant challenges for computational modeling.
papers.summary: This paper introduces TPT, a compact CNN-transformer hybrid model designed to efficiently model microbial small proteins, which are difficult to analyze due to their short length and rapid evolution. The model aims to improve computational prediction and analysis of these functionally important proteins.

papers.title: Representations of facial features and surface quality in monkey area TE compared to neural network models.
papers.abstract: The shape and spacing of facial features are essential for the perception of emotional expressions and the identification of individuals. The surface quality of faces, such as skin texture, eye twinkle, and hair gloss, is valuable for estimating health status. A previous fMRI study in monkeys revealed that regions selective for faces overlapped regions selective for object gloss in the central inferior temporal (IT) cortex, suggesting that the surface quality of faces is processed in area TE. However, the representation of facial surface quality has not been directly examined in this area. To
papers.summary: This study investigates how monkey area TE represents facial features and surface quality, comparing these representations to neural network models. The findings suggest that area TE encodes both facial shape and surface properties, with neural network models providing a useful comparison for understanding these representations.

papers.title: A generative AI multi-agent framework with integrated XAI governance for cancer diagnostics: from multi-omics interpretation to lifestyle risk stratification.
papers.abstract: Cancer diagnostics is being reshaped by rapid advances in artificial intelligence, yet a persistent gap separates computational performance from clinical trust. Systematic reviews confirm that 83% of XAI studies in oncology excluded clinicians from development or evaluation, 87% lacked rigorous assessment of XAI explanations, and no universally accepted quality metrics for XAI outputs currently exist. Concurrently, generative AI (GenAI) is entering oncology at an unprecedented pace, yet it operates largely without formal interpretability governance.
papers.summary: This paper proposes a generative AI multi-agent framework for cancer diagnostics that integrates explainable AI (XAI) governance to bridge the gap between computational performance and clinical trust. It addresses the lack of clinician involvement and rigorous XAI evaluation in oncology by embedding interpretability governance into the framework, which spans from multi-omics interpretation to lifestyle risk stratification.
